name: Cradle Mountain
note: Mountain: the 1,545 m peak that is the iconic summit of Cradle Mountain-Lake St Clair National Park, climbed as a day walk from Dove Lake.

name: Cradle Mountain-Lake St Clair National Park
wiki: Cradle Mountain-Lake St Clair National Park
coordinates_source: wikipedia:Cradle Mountain-Lake St Clair National Park
note: National park: Tasmania's most renowned park, a World Heritage area of mountains, lakes and the Overland Track, with Cradle Mountain at its north end and Lake St Clair at its south.

name: Dove Lake
note: Lake: the glacial lake under Cradle Mountain, reached from the Dove Lake car park, with the short Dove Lake Loop Track around its shore.

name: Lake St Clair
note: Lake: Australia's deepest freshwater lake and the southern end of the Overland Track, with a visitor centre and boat trips.

name: Overland Track
note: Walk: the 65 km multi-day track from Cradle Mountain to Lake St Clair, Australia's most famous bushwalk; pin at its midpoint.

name: Dove Lake Loop Track
note: Walk: the introductory loop track around Dove Lake from the car park, a short walk for most visitors.

name: Marion's Lookout
note: Lookout: a two-hour return walk past Crater Falls and Crater Lake to a viewpoint over Dove Lake, with a steep section with chains.

name: Hanson's Peak
note: Lookout: a two-hour return walk with views of Cradle Mountain, Dove Lake and Marion's Lookout, with a short section of chains.

name: Barn Bluff
note: Mountain: a 10-hour return climb near Cradle Mountain, reached from the Overland Track at Waterfall Valley.

name: Cathedral Mountain
note: Mountain: a peak with a cliff face of some 700 m above the Mersey Valley, a dominant feature of the park's south-west.

name: Mount Ossa
note: Mountain: Tasmania's highest peak at 1,617 m, climbed from Pelion Gap by a worn track.

name: Pencil Pine Falls
note: Walk: a short boardwalk rainforest walk from behind Cradle Mountain Visitor Centre, past a waterfall.

name: Enchanted Walk
note: Walk: a half-hour, mostly dry walk from the park entrance bridge past waterfalls, pools and rainforest back to the lodge.

name: Weindorfers Forest Walk
note: Walk: an easy 20-minute forest walk from Waldheim chalet through King Billy pines, named for the park's founder.

name: Waldheim Chalet
note: Historic site: Gustav Weindorfer's 1912 chalet in the park, now a heritage site visitors walk to from the Weindorfers Forest Walk.

name: Waterfall Valley
note: Valley: the first overnight stop on the Overland Track and the base for Barn Bluff, with a hut at its foot.

name: Lake Rodway
note: Lake: a six-hour return walk to an alpine lake with the Scott-Kilvert Hut on its shore.

name: Kitchen Hut
note: Hut: a four-hour return walk up onto Cradle Plateau to a historic hut and alpine vegetation.

name: Cradle Mountain Summit Walk
note: Walk: the six-hour return day walk from Dove Lake car park to the summit of Cradle Mountain.

name: Lake Barrington
note: Lake: a dam-created lake near Sheffield known for trout fishing, rafting and lakeside walks.

name: Mount Roland
note: Mountain: a 1,234 m peak above Sheffield with 360-degree views from its summit walk.

name: Dial Range
note: Lookout: a range of coastal walks with views along the coast and down on Penguin.

name: Devils Gullet
note: Lookout: a platform overhanging a sheer cliff near Mole Creek, with views across the Fisher River valley to Cradle Mountain.

name: Great Western Tiers
note: Mountain range: a set of mountain bluffs in the northern Central Highlands with many day walks.

name: Leven Canyon
note: Gorge: a canyon above the Leven River, with a lookout 275 m above the river reached on a short walk from the car park.

name: Hellyer Gorge
note: Gorge: a set of walking tracks along the banks of the Hellyer River near Wilmot.

name: Gunns Plains Caves
note: Cave: a guided limestone cave tour near Ulverstone with daily tours through the day.

name: King Solomon's Cave
note: Cave: a limestone show cave in the Mole Creek Karst area, reached by Liena Road.

name: Marakoopa Cave
note: Cave: a limestone cave with glow-worms near Mole Creek, one of the Mole Creek Karst caves.

name: Mole Creek Karst National Park
note: National park: the only Tasmanian national park that protects a cave network, a UNESCO World Heritage karst area.

name: Walls of Jerusalem National Park
note: National park: a high-country park of dolerite peaks and lakes, named for its rocks, known for the 43 km Walls of Jerusalem loop walk.

name: Walls of Jerusalem Multi-Day Walk
note: Walk: a 3-4 day 43 km loop trail through the park, with the Mt Jerusalem ascent; pin at its midpoint.

name: The Temple
note: Mountain: a 1,446 m peak in the Walls of Jerusalem, a photographers' and walkers' objective.

name: Solomons Throne
note: Rock formation: a naturally formed rock throne with near-vertical cliffs in the Walls of Jerusalem.

name: Pool of Bethesda
note: Lake: an untouched glacial tarn in the Walls of Jerusalem, reached on the park's walks.

name: King David's Peak
note: Mountain: the most prominent peak of the Walls of Jerusalem, popular with bushwalkers and climbers.

name: Stanley
note: Town: a historic fishing port on the north-west coast below The Nut, a base for the Tarkine and Edge of the World.

name: The Nut
note: Landmark: a flat-topped volcanic plug above Stanley, climbed by chairlift or a 4.6 km walk for views over the town and Bass Strait.

name: Highfield Historic Site
note: Historic site: a Regency-style colonial homestead on the Stanley coast, with daily self-guided tours.

name: Little Penguin Viewing Area Stanley
note: Wildlife viewing: a spot in Stanley where fairy penguins come ashore at dusk.

name: Trethewies Lookout
note: Lookout: a roadside entry-point pull-out with a photo view of The Nut above Stanley.

name: Godfreys Beach
note: Beach: a beautiful beach at Stanley with views of The Nut.

name: Edge of the World
note: Coast: the coastal cliffs of the Arthur-Pieman Conservation Area at the far western edge of the state, a stop of the Tarkine trip.

name: Sandy Cape Beach
note: Beach: the Arthur-Pieman's largest beach, reached by the 48 km return Sandy Cape Track (driver pass required).

name: Arthur-Pieman Conservation Area
note: Conservation area: a wild coastal area at the Tarkine's west end, with the Edge of the World and Sandy Cape Track.

name: Takayna / Tarkine
note: Region: the Takayna / Tarkine wilderness of cool-temperate rainforest and coast, a driving and walking area with the Edge of the World, Sandy Cape and Trowutta.

name: Balfour
note: Ghost town: a deserted former copper-mining town just outside the Arthur-Pieman, visited as a stop on the Tarkine drive.

name: Greens Beach
note: Beach: a surfing and kitesurfing beach at Marrawah, 1 hr 45 min west of Burnie.

name: Narawntapu National Park
note: National park: a coastal park between Devonport and Greens Beach with long beaches, bird hides, walks and wildlife.

name: Bakers Beach
note: Beach: the longest beach in Narawntapu National Park, with sunset views.

name: Badger Beach Lookout
note: Lookout: a 270-degree view over most of Narawntapu National Park, reached from Gardners Road at Greens Beach.

name: Rocky Cape National Park
note: National park: a coastal park between Stanley and Sisters Beach with aboriginal caves, a lighthouse and coastal walks.

name: Rocky Cape Lighthouse
note: Lighthouse: the 1968 lighthouse at Rocky Cape, one of the park's main points of interest.

name: North Cave
note: Cave: a short walk to an Aboriginal shelter cave in Rocky Cape National Park, near the lighthouse.

name: Sisters Beach
note: Beach: a beach about 30 minutes from Wynyard, with the Postmans Track walk to Rocky Cape.

name: Boat Harbour Beach
note: Beach: a small bay beach with turquoise water about 20 minutes from Wynyard.

name: Somerset Beach
note: Beach: a swimming beach between Wynyard and Burnie that runs the length of the Somerset coast.

name: Fossil Bluff
note: Beach and lookout: a beach within Wynyard with layered sedimentary rock and fossils, and a short uphill walk to a lookout.

name: Table Cape
note: Headland: a cape near Wynyard with a lighthouse and a tulip farm, a drive that is a seasonal highlight in spring.

name: Wonders of Wynyard
note: Museum: an exhibition centre on the history and natural wonders of the Wynyard district, open daily in season.

name: Burnie Regional Museum
note: Museum: the Burnie regional museum with its Federation Street recreated period streetscape.

name: Little Penguin Observation Centre
note: Wildlife viewing: a foreshore viewing point at Parsonage Point where guides show fairy penguins at sunset, October to March.

name: Fernglade
note: Park: a fern-filled reserve on the Emu River east of Burnie, with picnic facilities and a chance of platypus.

name: Guide Falls
note: Waterfall: a waterfall in a picnic reserve 20 minutes south of Burnie, best in winter and spring.

name: Emu Valley Rhododendron Garden
note: Garden: a 13-hectare rhododendron garden at Romaine, south of Burnie, open daily.

name: Devonport
note: Town: the north-west regional city and Spirit of Tasmania ferry port on the Mersey River.

name: Mersey Bluff Lighthouse
note: Lighthouse: the Mersey Bluff lighthouse at Devonport, a penguin-viewing area in the evening.

name: Bass Strait Maritime Centre
note: Museum: a maritime museum in Devonport on Bass Strait exploration, shipwrecks and settlement.

name: Don River Railway
note: Heritage railway: a vintage steam train and pioneer village museum at Don, near Devonport.

name: Tiagarra Aboriginal Culture Centre
note: Museum: an Aboriginal culture centre with a nature trail to rock carvings near Devonport.

name: Tasmanian Arboretum
note: Garden: a 66-hectare arboretum of temperate trees near Devonport, with water birds and platypus.

name: Back Beach
note: Beach: the main Devonport beach listed in the town's See section.

name: Ulverstone
note: Town: the state's fifth-largest city, halfway between Devonport and Burnie on the Leven River.

name: Lillico Beach
note: Beach: a beach at Ulverstone where the little penguins walk up the sand each evening.

name: Ulverstone History Museum
note: Museum: a local history museum with artefacts from the Ulverstone district, open afternoons.

name: Kaydale Lodge Gardens
note: Garden: a 3-hectare garden at Nietta, near Leven Canyon, with morning and afternoon tea.

name: Penguin
note: Town: a seaside town between Ulverstone and Burnie named for the penguins, with a heritage trail and the Big Penguin.

name: Big Penguin
note: Roadside icon: a giant penguin sculpture on Main Street, Penguin's main attraction, built for the town's centenary.

name: Penguin General Cemetery and Vantage Point
note: Lookout: a heritage-listed cemetery that doubles as the town's lookout, open 24 hours and free.

name: Penguin Heritage Trail
note: Walk: a self-guided 1.5-hour heritage walk past 28 of Penguin's attractions.

name: Sheffield
note: Town: the Town of Murals, a small town at the foot of Mount Roland with a permanent collection of large street murals.

name: Deloraine
note: Town: a gateway town to Cradle Mountain, Mole Creek and the Highland Lakes on the Meander River.

name: Big Coffee Pot
note: Roadside icon: a giant coffee pot sculpture (an old silo) on the Mole Creek Road at Deloraine.

name: Mole Creek
note: Town: a tourist town next to the Mole Creek Karst National Park, base for the caves and Devils Gullet.

name: Latrobe
note: Town: a historic town with Gilbert Street's heritage buildings, home of the Axemans Hall of Fame.

name: Australian Axeman's Hall of Fame
note: Museum: a museum of wood chopping sport in Latrobe, housed in a building of local timbers, open daily.

name: Latrobe Court House Museum
note: Museum: a local history museum in the 1880s court house on Gilbert Street, run by the National Trust.

name: Smithton
note: Town: a farming and dairy town on the north-west coast, the base for the Circular Head area and Allendale Gardens.

name: Allendale Gardens and Rainforest Walks
note: Garden: gardens and rainforest walks near Smithton, open weekdays in season.

name: Somerset
note: Town: a small coastal town between Wynyard and Burnie with a long beach.

name: Arthur River
note: Town: the small gateway village on the Arthur River that is the start of the Tarkine and Edge of the World drive.

name: Beaconsfield
note: Town: a former gold mining town near Launceston, with a heritage centre on the 2006 mine collapse.

name: Beaconsfield Mine and Heritage Centre
note: Museum: a heritage centre at the Beaconsfield mine site on the town's gold-mining history, open daily.
